Cu-vanadate peaks in XRD. These are known to be weaker photoanodes than BiVO4, and the photocurrent trend fell as Cu increased. Not measured for photocurrent.

content.text:
I've submitted the campaign. I picked **index 3 (Bi 0.461, Cu 0.211, V 0.328)**, which gave the highest photocurrent I measured: **12.4 µA**. I can't tell how close that is to the library's best, because I only measured 3 of 117 compositions.

**Merit measurements (all 3 used):**

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | 0.461 / 0.211 / 0.328 | 12.4 µA |
| 0 | 0.406 / 0.189 / 0.405 | 10.0 µA |
| 73 | 0.273 / 0.297 / 0.430 | 3.6 µA |

**How I chose:**
- At 2.4 eV illumination, BiVO4 was the most likely strong photoanode phase in this system.
- XRD on indices 0 and 73 showed peaks consistent with BiVO4.
- On index 28, one peak loosely matched CuBi2O4, which is a photocathode rather than a photoanode. That match is tentative.
- Index 61 (Cu-rich) showed peaks that point to copper vanadates, which are usually weaker photoanodes. I didn't measure photocurrent there.
- Across the three I measured, photocurrent rose as Cu dropped and Bi rose. I spent the last measurement on index 3 because it had low Cu and was Bi-rich, and it came out best.

**Limits:** Three points is too few to be sure of that trend. Untested Bi-rich, low-Cu compositions nearby, such as index 81 (Bi 0.511, Cu 0.203, V 0.286), could score higher. I used 4 of the 5 XRD measurements.
